 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C. PRAYING TO QUASH THE FIR IN CR.NO.249/2022 DATED 29.11.2022 REGISTERED BY THE RESPONDENT NO.1 DOBBASPET POLICE STATION PENDING BEFORE 2ND ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE BENGALURU RURAL DISTRICT, BENGALURU, FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 504, 420, 406, 120-B, 149 OF IPC, 1860 ALONG WITH SECTIONS 3(1)(f), 3(i)(r) AND 3(1)(s)
OF SC/ST ACT, 1989 ON A COMPLAINT FILED BY THE RESPONDENT NO.2 ON 29.11.2022 VIDE DOCUMENT NO.1.

THESE CRIMINAL PETITIONS HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR ORDERS ON 19.04.2023, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Crl.P.No.12025/2022 is filed by petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 6 and Crl.P.No.11929/2022 is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.7 and 8 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR in Crime No.249/2022 registered by the Dobbaspet Police Station, Nelamangala Circle, Bengaluru for the offences punishable under Sections 504, 420, 406, 120(B), 149 of IPC and Sections 3(i)(f), 3(i)(r)
and (s) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (for short 'SC/ST (POA) Act').
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that respondent No.2-complainant has filed a complaint on 29.11.2022 alleging that the Government has granted a land in favour of his father on 30.01.1982 in L.R.F.No.411/75-76 in Sompura Village measuring 4 acres 14 guntas in Survey No.110/2 and 3 guntas of kharab land.
After the death of his father, the properties were divided in the name of the children and wife.
In the year 2006, one Krishnareddy had agreement of sale for Rs.28,50,000/- per acre and received Rs.5.00 lakhs as advance and he has filed a civil suit against him.

Subsequently,
they compromised the case.
It was orally agreed to give 10 guntas.
There is no documents for the above said 10 guntas of land.
In order to register a document for 10 guntas of land, the accused took the complainant for preparing GPA, but, they got GPA for 2 acres of land instead of 10 guntas of land in the name of Nagaraj.
When the same was questioned by the complainant, the accused persons said to be abused them in filthy language by taking the name of the caste as Madiga.
Therefore, prayed for taking action against them.
Based upon the same, the Police registered the FIR and took up the investigation which is under challenge.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that there is no ingredient made out against the petitioners for attracting any of the provisions of IPC or SC/ST (POA) Act.
Therefore, prayed for quashing the FIR.

Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader as well as learned counsel for respondent No.2 objected the petition and contended that the investigation is under progress.
The accused persons abused the complainant with filthy language by taking the caste name and insulted the members of the SC/ST which attracts Section 3(1)(r), (s) and (f) of the SC/ST (POA) Act.

Hence,
prayed for dismissing the petition.
6. Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, the case of the complainant is that the land in survey No.110/2 has been granted to their father.

There was an agreement of sale with one Krishnareddy and thereafter, a case was filed against them and there was an oral mutual agreement where the complainant was ready to give 10 guntas of land and in order to execute the document for 10 guntas of land, the accused have manipulated the document by showing 2 acres of land.

The sale deed produced by the learned counsel for the petitioners reveals that there was GPA executed by the complainant and family in favour of one Nagaraj and the said Nagaraj said to be sold the property based upon the GPA.
The complainant claims that the said Nagaraj has created the documents and got executed for 2 acres of land instead of 10 guntas.
When the same came to the knowledge of the complainant and when they enquired with the accused persons, they have scolded, abused the complainant in filthy language by taking into the caste name.
Therefore, without going for the investigation, at this stage, the FIR cannot be quashed.
The Investigating Officer is required to examine the witnesses and the documents and file the final report.
The FIR is not an encyclopedia to show all the contents of the disputes until the Investigating Officer investigate the matter.

Therefore,
the petitioners are required themselves available for the investigation and until final report filed, the FIR cannot be quashed.
7. Accordingly, both the petitions filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 6 and 7 and 8 are hereby dismissed.
